text:
Rina: quick heads-up: we saw a discrepancy in route selection between sim and prod for a small tenant during peak yesterday. sim picked local-GPU, prod picked cold-fallback. not catastrophic but reproducible.
Sam: do we have the eval trace? any non-deterministic ops?
Rina: attached minimal trace. looks like rounding differences in the bucket aggregator plus an ordering variance when applying soft-pref boosts.
Devon: are we still using float32 accumulators in sim and int64 counters in prod? that could explain it.
Omar: yep, prod aggregates cost as integer microslots on the ingestion path to avoid float drift. sim has been optimized with float sums for speed.
Sam: two options: 1) make sim match prod's integer path exactly (slower), or 2) accept small diffs and add shadow-checkers that compare binary decisions and emit reconciliations.
Rina: leaning to 2) with an optional deterministic mode for nightly verification. shadow-checkers would run in parallel, sampling 0.1% and recording a compact reconciliation record.
Devon: what fields in reconciliation record? we should avoid leaking internal IDs to telemetry. propose: {seed_hash, route_hash, decision_delta_tag, small_numeric_summary}.
Omar: agree on redaction. also add a flag to keep full debug traces on a secure, time-limited request when customer impact is suspected.
Sam: implementation detail: shadow-checkers need to run synchronously at evaluation point but must be non-blocking for the request path. emit reconciliations async.
Rina: perf budget: shadow-checker cost must be < 2% p95 latency added for sampled requests. if we can't meet that, fall back to offline replay compare.
Devon: we should also stabilize the bucket semantics. propose adding `deterministic_bucketize` to the policy runtime that uses the prod integer semantics and documented tie-breaking rules. sim can call that path when `--deterministic` is enabled.
Sam: good. also worth adding unit tests that fuzz permutations of operations: `sum(bucketize(...))`, `bucketize(sum(...))`, and `interleave(prefers, penalties)` to detect non-associative behavior.
Omar: ops concerns: we need telemetry metrics: `policy.reconciliation.count`, `policy.reconciliation.rate_mismatch`, and `policy.reconciliation.latency_penalty`. alerts if mismatch rate > 0.05% of sampled requests or more than baseline*4.
Rina: privacy: reconciliation payloads must never include tenant prompt text or PII. canonicalize route descriptors to opaque IDs.
Devon: DSL question: should we expose deterministic primitives in the public policy DSL or keep them internal? exposing helps advanced users reproduce, but widens surface area.
Sam: compromise: expose them as an "advanced" opt-in flag in policy manifest, default off. document strong warnings and limit to dedicated/private deployments only.
Omar: rollout: 1) implement shadow-checker + redaction (canary 1), 2) add deterministic_bucketize and unit tests (canary 2), 3) enable nightly deterministic sim run and reconcile job (prod-scan).
Rina: canary plan: enable sampling at 0.1% in `dev` for 24h, then `staging` 1% for 48h, then `canary-rtg` 0.5% for 24h. auto-rollback on reconciliation spike > 100/hr or p95 latency regressions.
Devon: code owners: I'll pick up `deterministic_bucketize` PR. Sam take the shadow-checker PR. Omar wire alerts and ops playbook. Rina will draft the policy manifest wording.
ops-bot: reminder: schedule canary windows via infra for 3490003600-3490007200.
Sam: noted, I'll open the PRs and link them here.
Rina: one more: add a tiny explain hook that returns the `decision_delta_tag` only when debug-flag is enabled so we can correlate customer reports without leaking details to the UI.
Omar: make sure the explain hook respects feature flags and tenant ACLs.
Devon: will add tests and a small sim harness job that runs permutations every night and posts a weekly reconciliation report to #architecture.
Rina: thanks team. I'll follow up with a short RFC draft and the canary schedule.
